assessment:
SOURCE 1–2 show the same elongated building from the ramp end and an adjoining long side: a recessed lower structure, projecting glazed upper perimeter, external ramp flights and a roof dipping between unequal raised edges. SOURCE 3 shows ground-level glazing, columns and exposed beams supporting the perimeter walkway. SOURCE 4 shows the curved timber ceiling, internal spiral stair and open interior. SOURCE 5 and 8 provide sections showing the roof, surrounding buffer zone and unequal internal floor relationships; SOURCE 5 and 7 also provide plans. SOURCE 6 distinguishes the retained frame, timber addition and lightweight outer enclosure. These shared landmarks establish one building; no numerical dimensions are user-confirmed here.

CURRENT retains the recognizable arrangement, but the ramp end reads as congested overlapping diagonals, and heavy dark linework obscures the source’s lightweight enclosure and structural hierarchy. The roof’s dipping end profile is present; a missing curved roof is not supported by these images. Current views are small and largely canonical, so exact bay counts, ramp landing connections, glazing joints and internal section relationships remain uncertified. Apparent crossings cannot establish physical intersections, and no intended shadow gap can be certified.

issues.problem: SOURCE 1–2 show distinct ramp flights with readable deck edges, railings and intermediate landings. CURRENT 11 compresses these into overlapping diagonal bands, with projecting ends whose connections to the perimeter platforms are unclear.
issues.action: Locally check and correct flight elevations, lateral separation and landing alignment against the source ramp-end view. Each flight must terminate at its intended platform with continuous deck and railing connections. Confirm actual clashes before changing geometry; preserve any correctly aligned flight.

issues.problem: SOURCE 1–3 show slender pale framing, transparent glazing and visually distinct floor edges. CURRENT 9–12 and 14 read as a dense black cage, obscuring openings and the separation between the outer enclosure and recessed structure. These screenshots cannot distinguish excessive member thickness from accumulated edges or display settings.
issues.action: First obtain a closer source-aligned view with restrained edge display. Then locally correct only confirmed oversized or duplicate framing and incorrect visible materials, retaining pale structural members, transparent glazing and clear floor-edge hierarchy.

keep: Central downward curvature and unequal raised edges of the roof end profile.
Visible separation of the projecting upper enclosure from the recessed ground-level frontage.
